A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ring-C modifications of colchicine did not affect the cytotoxic activity of colchicine against PC-3 cells, but did affect the cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells, which is consistent with the results obtained from the in vitro microtubular assembly assay.

the C-1 and C-2 positions of the A-ring of colchicine can be modified without affecting the cytotoxic activity of this compound, while modifications at the C-7 position of the B-ring of colchicines lead to loss of activity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ring-C of colchicine is a critical structural feature for colchicine to bind tubulin and inhibit tubulin polymerization.
ring-C modifications of colchicine are possible in a regio- and stereo-controlled fashion and that the products are cytotoxic and can serve as prodrugs.
ring-C modifications of colchicine can have an impact on its biological activity, which may provide new insights for the development of more selective and effective colchicine analogues.
